issues.legal_issue: Secondary evidence of a public judgment is admissible when the original has been lost and the statutory conditions for secondary evidence are met.
material_facts: The community offered an ordinary copy of the judgment in an earlier suit to establish its contents.
The original judgment was no longer available in the court records, and the certified copy obtained by the community had been lost.
The opposing parties did not deny that the earlier judgment existed or claim that the copy offered was inaccurate.
issues.conclusion: The ordinary copy of the earlier judgment was admissible as secondary evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 65(c) of the Evidence Act, secondary evidence may be given when the original has been lost. That provision operates independently of Section 65(f), so secondary evidence may be admitted even for a public document when the conditions of clause (c) are fulfilled. The Court relied on Mst. Bibi Aisha v. The Bihar Sunni Majlis Avaqaf, AIR 1969 SC 253.

predicates.civil_proceeding: A party is offering documentary evidence in a civil proceeding.
predicates.public_judgment_copy_offered: A party offers a copy of a judgment that is a public document to prove its contents.
predicates.original_lost: The original document has been lost or destroyed.

issues.definition: When a party offers a copy of a public judgment in a civil proceeding and the original has been lost, ordinary secondary evidence is admissible.

issues.legal_issue: A final judgment between the parties that determined title binds them in a later suit concerning the same title.
material_facts: In an earlier contested suit, the community's title to the property was affirmed by a competent court, and the judgment became final.
The earlier suit included the respondents, with the minor respondent represented by his mother, who was also a party in her individual capacity.
The earlier judgment determined that the respondents and their predecessor possessed the property as Pujaris, not as owners.
The respondents again claimed ownership through their predecessor in the later suit.
issues.conclusion: The earlier judgment was binding on the respondents, who were precluded from denying the community's title.
issues.legal_principle: The principle of res judicata precludes parties from relitigating a matter of title that was finally decided between them by a competent court. The Court applied that principle to the final judgment in the earlier suit.

predicates.later_suit_about_same_title: A party brings a later suit concerning title to property that was at issue in an earlier suit.
predicates.prior_final_judgment_between_parties: A competent court issued a final judgment between the parties, including any party properly represented in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.prior_judgment_determined_title: The earlier judgment determined which party held title to the property.

issues.definition: A final determination of title between parties binds them in a later suit when that suit concerns the same title.

issues.legal_issue: Possession that was held in a permissive or non-owner capacity does not establish adverse possession unless the claimant pleads and proves when and how it became open, hostile, and adverse.
material_facts: The earlier final judgment established that the respondents and their predecessor possessed the property as Pujaris and that their claim of ownership had been rejected.
The respondents claimed adverse possession based on the predecessor's alleged ownership and long possession.
The respondents neither pleaded nor proved that their possession became adverse after the earlier judgment, or the time and manner of any such change.
issues.conclusion: The respondents did not establish title by adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: Where possession was initially held in a non-owner capacity and a competent court has rejected the possessor's claim of title, the claimant must allege and prove that the possession later became open, hostile, and adverse, including the time and manner of the change. Possession alone, without proof of that change, does not establish adverse title.

predicates.adverse_possession_claim: A party claims title to property through adverse possession.
predicates.prior_judgment_established_nonowner_poss: A prior final judgment established that the claimant or predecessor possessed the property in a non-owner capacity.
predicates.no_pleaded_or_proved_hostile_conversion: The claimant neither pleads nor proves when and how that possession became open, hostile, and adverse.

issues.definition: A claim based on possession previously established as non-owner possession fails when the claimant neither pleads nor proves how and when that possession became hostile.
